description: Repair four lying surfaces (cam-plan.md twins, CONTEXT.md glossary, patterns.md oracle-authoring block, orchestrator boot prompt) so every agent-read artifact agrees with the shipped code, and close the CAM-431 configPath seam at the same two call sites.

userStories.title: Gate the orchestrator boot prompt on worker_isolation and forward configPath at both call sites
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator booting a session, I need the boot prompt's autonomous-mode instruction to be emitted only when auto-dispatch is actually armed (meta_loop=auto AND worker_isolation=container), so that my very first user turn stops contradicting the sidecar's own auto-chaining guard and the agent persona body.
acceptanceCriteria: buildOrchestratorBootPrompt consults worker_isolation in addition to meta_loop, so the 'auto' branch emits the 'proceed directly into dispatch' instruction only when the sidecar would actually arm auto-chaining. The reference PIN for the gate condition is src/commands/sidecar.ts:2944-2953 (meta_loop=auto plus worker_isolation!=container disables auto-chaining); do NOT change that sidecar behavior, only make the prompt agree with it. Oracle is scoped to the function body, not the file, because readWorkerIsolation is already imported at run.ts:64 and already used at run.ts:872 in a different function. [oracle: sed -n '/export function buildOrchestratorBootPrompt/,/^}/p' src/commands/run.ts | grep -q 'readWorkerIsolation']

A behavioral test in test/commands/run-boot-prompt-isolation.test.ts proves BOTH sides of the gate against real project.toml fixtures written into a real tmpdir (no mocked config reader): with meta_loop=auto plus worker_isolation=host the prompt does NOT contain the proceed-directly-into-dispatch instruction, and with meta_loop=auto plus worker_isolation=container it does. Every test name in the file must be free of parentheses, because 'bun test -t' treats its argument as a REGEX. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/commands/run-boot-prompt-isolation.test.ts -t 'boot prompt' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && ! echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* fail']

Both production call sites forward configPath instead of calling with no argument, closing the CAM-431 seam residue at the exact sites this story already touches. The signature already accepts configPath (src/commands/run.ts:225); the defect is the two call sites at src/commands/run.ts:584 and src/commands/setup.ts:551, each of which already has a cwd in scope. [oracle: ! grep -qE 'buildOrchestratorBootPrompt\(\)' src/commands/run.ts src/commands/setup.ts]

The stale comment in test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts, which claims there is no configPath seam on that site, is corrected to state that readBackend does accept configPath (src/config/models.ts:224). The comment text is BROKEN ACROSS TWO LINES in the file, so the comparand is the short substring, not the whole sentence. [oracle: ! grep -q 'no configPath seam' test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts]

The pre-existing boot-prompt suite in test/run.test.ts stays green: its meta_loop=auto case at test/run.test.ts:808 writes a fixture with NO worker_isolation key (which defaults to host) and asserts the prompt contains 'autonomous', so under the new gate it must be updated to write worker_isolation = "container" in the fixture rather than deleted or weakened. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/run.test.ts 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && ! echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* fail']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]

userStories.title: Add the CLI-oracle rule to the curated oracle-authoring block in patterns.md
userStories.description: As whoever authors an acceptance criterion for this repo, I need the curated oracle-authoring block to carry the rule that a CLI-behavior oracle invokes 'bun index.ts <sub>' and never 'cam <sub>', so that oracles stop measuring the installed binary instead of the working tree and stop going red for the wrong artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: The curated oracle-authoring block in scripts/cam/patterns.md gains a fifth numbered rule stating that an oracle checking CLI behavior invokes 'bun index.ts <sub>' and never 'cam <sub>', because 'cam' measures the INSTALLED binary, which is almost always older than the change under test. Oracle is scoped to the curated block, not the file, and requires the literal 'bun index.ts' on the same physical line as the '5.' marker, because the token already appears 3 times elsewhere in the file so a global grep would be tautological. [oracle: sed -n '/CURATED BLOCK: oracle authoring rules/,$p' scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]+5\. .*bun index\.ts']

EVIDENCE FIDELITY, which is rule 4 of the block applied to the block itself: rule 5 carries the MEASURED evidence token, not a plausible restatement of the problem. The measurement is CAM-449 AC7, where the installed binary at version 0.262.0 returned a plannable set different from the working tree's, turning the criterion red for the wrong artifact and inducing the documented mid-cycle rebuild hazard. [oracle: grep -q '0\.262\.0' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The block's own preamble stops saying there are four rules once a fifth exists, so the header does not become a new lying surface. The phrase 'These four rules are what those cycles measured' occurs exactly once in the file today, inside that preamble. [oracle: ! grep -q 'These four rules' scripts/cam/patterns.md]
